ratings.comment: Professor Zhu is a nice guy, but his class is way too hard for how it should be. Labs are hard to follow and I'm rather chasing the way too general instructions most of the time instead of learning GIS skills. No clear lab grading criteria, which is rough when it makes up most of your grade. Would not recommend.

A-Xing seems passionate about his field, but this does not translate well into his teaching skills. Online lectures are extremely dry. His accent is difficult to understand, and no reliable subtitles are provided. Exam questions had many grammatical errors and some did not make sense at all. Lectures also haven't been updated since 2020.

The class is fun and the material that he presents is very educational. The lecture videos are also pretty solid. However, his English writing makes it very challenging to understand the exam questions and the written lectures. In addition, a lot of the class is just memorizing what he says is the correct answer in his lectures.

He is obviously very passionate about GIS and really wants to make sure his students know what's going on "under the hood" with many of the spatial methods and tools that he covers. The broken English that he uses in his readings and tests can be irritating, but as long as you understand the material you'll do fine. Very nice guy and truly cares.

He seems to be a nice guy, but with broken English in lectures and quizzes, which make it so hard, boring and despair for me. The quiz is like choose the most correct but with the broken English (you know it's gonna be nightmare).

Seems like a nice guy, but his lectures were so boring. It takes days for assignments to be graded and you don't really know what you have in the class for the whole semester. Exams were pretty difficult and the grading for them is pretty harsh.

He is terrible at explaining things and hard to understand, lectures put me to sleep even though they were online.  Lab directions were clear but are extremely frustrating, especially if you have never used ArcGIS before.  I would recommend taking 370 before this class.  I love the topics but he made it so boring.

I had him for 377 and currently have him for 579. There's an online textbook which I believe he wrote himself, since he always credits his work in it. You must read this to understand what's happening in class. He's obviously a smart guy but the content is incredibly boring and there's a lot of broken english in the textbook, which makes it hard.

Prof Zhu is a great professor who is passionate about GIS. He presents topics very clearly in lecture. Lecture is not required, but you will not do well in the class if you do not go. You need to do the work to do well. The tests are very difficult, there are pop quizzes, and lab attendance is required. The class is slightly curved.

A-Xing is super nice and really cares about the subject. He get's really into the lectures and his mannerisms are very cute. The topics can get boring, but he tries to simplify them as much as possible and tries hard to get them across. Has a good attitude about learning and school.

Labs very useful and applicable but lectures suck. 2 power lectures (75 min)/week and eventually stopped going. Very enthusiastic about the topic however usually strays off topic to boast how the U.S. has much better GIS than the rest of the world and he is often wrong on these tangents. 5 pop-quizzes worth 5pts each. Exams have obscure questions
Exams are tough. He is passionate about the subject. Most of the time lectures are good!

His lectures are pretty good because he is very passionate about his field. However, sometimes his lectures can be a bit boring as he goes on in excessive detail about things that often you are not interested in related to GIS. The exams are tough. He grades them hard. Labs are time-consuming but easy.

An excellent professor. There's a lot of class material and it can get dry at times, but he explains it clearly, enthusiastically, references real life examples/relevant stories to make it more interesting, and is happy to help during office hours. His accent is about on par with Martin Yan(TV chef), so its nothing to worry about. Solid overall.

I had Axing for 579 and 377. I think he is a good professor and disagree with the reviews that say he is unclear. He explains most concepts very well. The issue is that there is a lot of material to cover and some concepts are just difficult to grasp. Go to class, think through the labs, and study for the exams and you will easily get an A.

A-xing is friendly, yet is truly a terrible teacher. His accent makes him difficult to understand and he has a very rambling way of lecturing, so it's very difficult to follow. He's incredibly bad at explaining complicated topics. Had him for Intro to GIS, Spatial Analysis, and GIS Apps; had to teach myself.  Wish there was a different professor.

Great Class - Very insightful abt the process of GIS applications and scientific thought, Had a lot of cross over into other course work. He is a very enthusiastic instructor about his topic. Labs were a bit long but the lectures were great.

Great instructor. You can tell he seriously knew the material. He was difficult to understand at times because of chinese accent but it never got in the way. Very comfortable with questions and always willing to help. The class was challenging, not because of Zhu, there was simply a lot of material. Definitely not a class you can skip often though

The only part I liked about this class was the lab. The lectures were boring and sometimes hard to understand because of 1-A-xing's accent and 2-the fact that he is just bad at explaining things in a way that can be understood. I would NOT recommend taking 377 if A-xing is the professor. It was painful.

It's unfortunate that Dr. Zhu is supposedly a great UW prof, when he's never there.  Seriously, he's never around.  Our TA taught our class way more than him.  But, our TA was a better prof than him.  The classes could be interesting , but he has a way of making it seem like you actually don't want to learn this stuff.
No Comments
